pluss::note::perm¶

Back to Note Factory API Reference

Signatures¶

Note pluss::note::perm(string_view word, std::int64_t pick,
                       WordSelectMode mode = WordSelectMode::Combination,
                       bool with_replacement = false,
                       bool unique_results = true)

WordSelectMode is pluss::note::WordSelectMode, an enum with values Combination and Permutation.

Combinations And Permutations Of A Word’s Characters¶

perm() enumerates length-pick selections of the characters of word and returns them as a rank-1 Note, one selection per cell. It is a combinatorial generator: anagram and word-game candidate lists, brute-force key spaces over a small alphabet, test corpora that need every arrangement of a set of letters.

The characters of word are treated positionally — the pool is “the characters at positions 0..n-1”, not “the distinct letters”. Repeated letters in word therefore contribute multiple pool entries; whether that surfaces as duplicate output strings depends on unique_results.

Parameters¶

  • word — the character pool, taken in left-to-right order.

  • pick — how many characters each selection contains. Must be >= 0. pick == 0 yields a single empty selection ([""]). Without replacement, pick greater than word.size() is impossible and yields an empty Note (not an error).

  • mode:

    • WordSelectMode::Combination (default) — order does not matter; each selection keeps word’s left-to-right order and picks strictly forward. "abc", pick 2 → ab, ac, bc.

    • WordSelectMode::Permutation — order matters; every arrangement is emitted. "abc", pick 2 → ab, ac, ba, bc, ca, cb.

  • with_replacement — when true, a position may be reused within one selection, so pick can exceed word.size(). "ab", pick 2, combination, with replacement → aa, ab, bb.

  • unique_results — when true (default), identical output strings are collapsed to their first occurrence; when false, every selection the enumeration produces is kept, including duplicates that arise from repeated letters in word.

The result is rank 1 and UTF-8 mode, in the order the enumeration visits selections (depth-first over word’s positions). perm is deterministic — there is no seed.

The count grows combinatorially with word.size() and pick. Keep both small; this is a generator for tens or hundreds of results, not millions.

Example 1: Combinations (Order Ignored)¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::note::perm("abc", 2)) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["ab", "ac", "bc"]

The three ways to choose 2 of 3 characters, each in word order.

Example 2: Permutations (Order Matters)¶

const pluss::Note n =
    pluss::note::perm("abc", 2, pluss::note::WordSelectMode::Permutation);
std::cout << n << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[6], dim=1, numel=6, encoding=utf8)
["ab", "ac", "ba", "bc", "ca", "cb"]

Every ordered arrangement of 2 characters.

Example 3: With Replacement¶

pluss::note::print(
    std::cout,
    pluss::note::perm("ab", 2, pluss::note::WordSelectMode::Combination, true))
    << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["aa", "ab", "bb"]

A position may repeat within a selection, so pick is not capped at word.size().

Example 4: Repeated Letters Are Deduplicated By Default¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::note::perm("aab", 2)) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2], dim=1, numel=2, encoding=utf8)
["aa", "ab"]

The pool is a, a, b. The positional enumeration produces aa, ab, ab; unique_results = true keeps the first of each — aa, ab.

Example 5: Keeping Every Selection¶

const pluss::Note n = pluss::note::perm(
    "aab", 2, pluss::note::WordSelectMode::Combination, false, false);
std::cout << n << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[3], dim=1, numel=3, encoding=utf8)
["aa", "ab", "ab"]

unique_results = false keeps the duplicate ab that the two a positions generate.

Example 6: pick Of Zero¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::note::perm("abc", 0)) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
[""]

Exactly one selection of length zero: the empty string.

Example 7: pick Larger Than The Word¶

const pluss::Note n = pluss::note::perm("abc", 4);
std::cout << n << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[0], dim=1, numel=0, encoding=utf8)
[]

Without replacement there is no way to choose 4 from 3 characters, so the result is an empty rank-1 Note — not an error. (With with_replacement = true it would instead enumerate all length-4 selections.)

See Also¶

  • pluss::note::rand: random letters rather than an exhaustive enumeration.

  • pluss::note::arange: a single ordered run of characters.

  • pluss::note::from_words: build a Note from words that already exist in a string.
